sessionTitle: Apply orchestration patterns for production AI agents

announcements.name: UiPath conversational agents now run in Microsoft Teams
announcements.shortDescription: agents built in UiPath via integration service connectors can be deployed through standard Teams packaging for one-on-one chats or channel-based workflows.
announcements.longDescription: UiPath agents, built and deployed in UiPath using its extensive integration service connectors, can now run inside Microsoft Teams. Once built, an agent is deployed via a standard Teams packaging process, after which employees can use it in one-on-one chats or in channel-based workflows. Employees can submit information, check process status, and receive updates all without leaving Teams.

announcements.name: GitHub Copilot integration via NPM-installed UiPath skills and CLI
announcements.shortDescription: installing the skills gives Copilot full context on the platform's APIs, CLI commands, and deployment patterns so developers can build and deploy without leaving Visual Studio Code.
announcements.longDescription: Copilot can now unlock the capabilities of the UiPath platform. Developers install the UiPath skills and CLI using NPM, which gives Copilot full context about the platform's APIs, CLI commands, and deployment patterns. From that point, developers can build, deploy, and manage their agentic automations on UiPath using their preferred coding agent.

announcements.name: Maestro Flow, a new developer canvas
announcements.shortDescription: a visual canvas backed by the Maestro runtime with a schema natively supported by coding agents, allowing local files, Git version control, and inline agent configuration.
announcements.longDescription: Maestro Flow is a new developer-friendly visual canvas whose runtime is Maestro, providing the same enterprise-grade governance, auditability, and durability. Unlike similar visual layers, this canvas comes with a schema that is natively supported by coding agents, so an agent can write the entire file and affect everything in Flow. In Visual Studio Code, the local files for Flow live on the developer's machine, allowing use of any coding agent and review of changes via Git or other version control.

announcements.name: Evaluations for end-to-end processes in Flow
announcements.shortDescription: test-case-style evaluations applied to whole process orchestrations, not just individual agents.
announcements.longDescription: UiPath announced bringing evaluations to end-to-end processes in Flow. These can be thought of as test cases for entire process orchestrations, extending the concept of evaluations previously used with individual agents. The goal is to combine an enjoyable developer experience with the power of an enterprise platform.

announcements.name: Maestro Case for complex exception-driven processes
announcements.shortDescription: a canvas where stages activate dynamically via case-manager rules or agent reasoning, supporting parallel work, re-entry, and escalations without explicit arrows.
announcements.longDescription: Maestro Case is a new canvas purpose-built for the dynamic, exception-driven work done in enterprises, going beyond straight-line BPMN. A Case Manager sits on top, with the case organized into stages and tasks (agents, API workflows, RPA, BPM, and external agents) under each. After the intake stage there are no arrows; each stage is activated based on what the case manager decides, either via rules or agent reasoning, supporting rework, parallel work such as underwriting and escalation running at once, re-entering stages, and escalations without losing continuity.

announcements.name: Agentic testing in UiPath Test Cloud
announcements.shortDescription: three capabilities: autonomous test execution with Autopilot (across Playwright, Appium, SAP, Epic, Citrix), autonomous test exploration, and UiPath Delegate for QA administrative work.
announcements.longDescription: UiPath's agentic testing solution in Test Cloud delivers three capabilities with one mission of autonomous software testing. First, autonomous test case execution with UiPath's Autopilot runs manual tests with no pre-built automations, executing across the web with Playwright, mobile with Appium, or any other UI such as SAP, Epic, and Citrix. Second, autonomous test exploration takes a mission and returns full coverage plans including edge cases; third, UiPath Delegate eliminates the administrative busy work that QA and testing teams handle today.

announcements.name: Availability
announcements.shortDescription: the CLI and skills are live now with GitHub Copilot support; Maestro Flow is in early access, publicly available in the coming weeks.
announcements.longDescription: Cliff Simpkins summarized that everything shown is available now or in early access. The UiPath CLI and skills are both live now with full GitHub Copilot support, and Maestro Flow [inferred] is in early access and will be publicly available in the coming weeks. Developers can install the CLI, add the UiPath skills to GitHub Copilot, and start building on the platform without leaving Visual Studio Code, with everything needed to get started at uipath.com/developers.
